subject: [R GSoC] Student Applications are finalized: Next Steps

messages.author: b98e21751c27e8b9
messages.subject: [R GSoC] Student Applications are finalized: Next Steps
parts:
All,

Thank you for a really great crop of potential student applications.
The final applications we received ahead of the deadline are really
outstanding.

Students:

I know you want to know *right now*, but project slot awards won't be
announced until May 6th. Please don't ask us whether you'll be
accepted, or what your chances of acceptance are, because program rules
prohibit us from telling you. Google grants slots to the organization,
and we will allocate those slots. Google reserves for itself the
notification of acceptance, rejection, and then pass/fail on each
evaluation.

Some of the students on this list may still have paperwork to finalize
with Google. If you have any steps that are still provisional, watch
the summerofcode website and your email very carefully, and follow up
with the Google systems as soon as you can. Many years, we lose
another promising student or two to trailing paperwork. Please be
diligent about deadlines. Google's deadlines are firm.

Mentors:

This is one of the busiest times for the R GSoC mentor community. Now
we need every one of our mentors to start evaluating the proposals
we've received. We encourage you to comment on any proposal where you
feel you have some expertise. The comments made on the summerofcode
website are only visible to the R mentor community. They are not
visible to the students. Please add your comments only there, and *do
not* discuss student proposals in any open forum (like this list). If
there is something sensitive you want to discuss, please bring it up in
an email to me and to Toby, and we will work with you on it.

Many of our project ideas have received multiple proposals. For your
project ideas with multiple proposals, we need you to voice an opinion
on the ranking of those proposals. Not just the first choice, but
second choice and reject recommendations as well. Students can and do
apply to multiple projects, and not only R. We need to know how to
value them in a competing priority world.

For project ideas that you will be a mentor for, please select 'Want to
Mentor' on the project page. For us to slot a project, all listed
mentors must select 'Want to Mentor' and comment on the proposal (we
need clear engagement from our mentors as well!).

You may see stars show up and disappear on the proposals. None of
these things are final yet, we are just using them to keep track of how
many slots we should request from Google.

Slot *requests* are due to Google April 22nd. We will not request a
slot for a project proposal that is not commented on by all of the
project mentors.

If you need additional mentors added to the system, or have questions
for me and Toby, please email us as soon as possible.

As always, if potential students or mentors have questions or issues,
you know where to find us.

Regards,

Brian
